files.interviews/summary.md:
# Restaurant manager interviews (5), Oct 2026

Who: general managers of independent restaurants, 15 to 60 staff, US (Austin, Denver, Chicago).

Top pains, in their words:
1. "Sunday night I build next week's rota in a spreadsheet and it takes 3 hours." (5 of 5)
2. "Shift swaps happen in a group chat and I find out when someone doesn't show." (4 of 5)
3. "I never know labour cost against sales until the month is over." (3 of 5)
4. "Tip pooling is a mess." (2 of 5)

Tools they use today: 7shifts (2), Homebase (2), When I Work (1), spreadsheets (all).

# Team notes

- In anything we might share outside the team, never name rivals: call them Rival A, B, C.
- Our working name is "Rota".

cases.notes: Interviews give the persona, the market and the rivals (the tools they use). CLAUDE.md gives the rival-name rule. A good intake states these and asks few questions (how bold, what we have today).

cases.ask: Benchmark us against Coupa, SAP Ariba, Jaggaer and Zip on intake-to-procure. We already have intake forms, approval routing and a supplier portal. I need a comprehensive capability matrix my VP of Procurement can read.
cases.notes: Enterprise procurement. Rivals, what we have, depth (comprehensive) and the main output (matrix) are all given. The reader (VP) is given. Good intake: asks group words and market at most.

cases.ask: what are rivals doing in AI note taking?
cases.notes: Vague: no product, no decision, no rivals, no persona. A good intake drafts a decision and a product line as defaults, proposes rivals found by search, and keeps to the question cap.

cases.ask: Precisamos decidir os módulos de um app de estoque para farmácias no Brasil. Rivals? not sure, find them. Portuguese sources are fine.
cases.notes: Mixed Portuguese and English. Market and source language are given. Rivals must be found. A good intake answers in the person's mix or plain English, names a rival-finding default, and may flag local rules (ANVISA, controlled drugs).

cases.ask: Compare Calendly, Cal.com and SavvyCal on team scheduling - pricing pages and help docs only. 20 minutes tops.
cases.notes: Tight time box and fixed source kinds. Quick track fits. The intake must not grow the scope (no reviews, no changelogs) and should keep the questions to one or two.

# Brief: employee onboarding tools

Decision: the first modules of an onboarding product for HR teams at 200 to 2,000 person companies.
Persona: HR operations manager who runs onboarding for 10 to 40 new starters a month. Pays: Head of People.
Rivals: BambooHR, HiBob, Personio.
Market: UK and Ireland.
Sources: product pages, help centre, release notes, pricing, public reviews.
How bold: both.
Out folder: research/onboarding/
